classification.difficultyReason: Find the eastward distance of a bearing leg using a right triangle, then add the due-east leg.

content.prompt:
A helicopter flies on a bearing of $140^\circ$ for $210\text{ km}$ then flies due east for $175\text{ km}$.
How far east (to the nearest kilometre) has the helicopter travelled from its starting point?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13 compass rose below the prompt
spec.description: Blank compass rose with four arrowheads and N, E, S, W labels. The source blue centre mark is rendered black under the ordinary diagram-mark convention.
spec.mathematics: North is upward, east rightward, south downward and west leftward. No flight legs, distances or angles are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student-visible drawing scaffold; no supplied answers.

answer.worked:
The first flight leg is $140^\circ-90^\circ=50^\circ$ south of east. In the right-angled triangle, let $x$ be its eastward distance.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 50^\circ &= \frac{x}{210}\\x &= 210\cos 50^\circ\end{align*}$$
The total eastward distance is
$$\begin{align*}d &= 210\cos 50^\circ+175\\d &\approx 310\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
